utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you are to make your opening statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the leave of the Court, we will not be making an opening statement. And to the effect that that waives our opportunity to make the opening statement, I simply must reaffirm what I stated, is that, you know, one of the attorney's duties in an opening statement is to say what the evidence will show in the case in chief, and the attorney involved needs to be familiar enough with his own evidence to make in good faith a statement as to what I can expect the evidence will show. Our 65 ter summaries take a stab at that, but even our own generation of those 65 ter summaries is based on hearsay and preparations that went on and that went on -- our case investigations that we now know are part of a criminal contempt investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you going a make an opening statement or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you're not, very well, call your first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not have a witness available pursuant to the witness difficulties. Mr. Ivetic traveled to the Balkans over the weekend to facilitate interviewing our potential witnesses and whatnot. The best we can get with our witnesses is someone in -- that will be coming in I believe tomorrow? Tomorrow, available for Wednesday. Excuse me. Tomorrow and Wednesday, available for Wednesday and Thursday. And that is the best we have, Your Honour. I raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That best is simply not good enough, Mr. Alarid. Did you not file, as was required, a list of the witnesses that you'd be calling, and there was one, I believe, for today after your opening statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, tell me precisely why that witness is not available.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because the necessary documentation and procedures that are required by the Witness and Victims, we were not able to get that done considering how stretched thin we are, Your Honour. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why is that, Mr. Alarid? Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Victims and Witnesses have reported to the Trial Chamber the difficulties based upon their inability to get the witness here. It's not a matter of the Defence of Milan Lukic not being able to get this first witness here, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask for the Victims and Witnesses Unit to be represented here and to provide the explanation. May I ask the registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand that there is a representative from the Victims and Witnesses Unit, and I will ask him, Mr. De Witt, to address the Court on this matter. MR. DE WITT: Your Honours, my name is Gus De Witt. I'm the chief of the Witness and Victims Section, and I would like to explain what has happened in terms of the first few witnesses that the Defence of Milan Lukic have scheduled for this week. What I may explain is it's a series of e-mails, communication between the Milan Lukic Defence team and the Victims and Witnesses trial assistant who makes the logistical arrangements for the arrival of witnesses. There are three witnesses which we were informed were scheduled for this week by the Milan Lukic Defence team, and I'm just looking at the Defence team just to ensure that I can mention their names. I believe they are not protected witnesses so I will --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They are actually protected witnesses. Two of them are, one is not. Two are protected, one is not. MR. DE WITT: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move into private session because I want a full explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid and Mr. Ivetic, I am distressed by what I have heard. Absolutely distressed. Mr. Ivetic, you led me to believe that this was a matter that was up to the Victims and Witnesses Unit. It is entirely your fault --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- for notifying the Victims and Witnesses Unit so late. Even the 10th of December is late for a witness to be present in court today. So you have absolutely no excuse, and let me make myself pellucidly clear: I will not put up with that from you anymore. You have a solemn duty to defend the accused Milan Lukic, and I am going to see to it that you discharge it. Otherwise, you will face the penalties. How can you expect to have witnesses here when you notify the Victims and Witnesses Unit on Friday last week? What do you think they are? What do you think they are? Do you think they pull the witnesses out of a hat?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, well, I think the Witnesses and Victims Unit are -- specifically are this: Human beings that are under the same constraints that we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Listen to me. Listen to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have cut you off. I have cut you off. I am not putting up with slackness like this in my court. I want you to understand that. That is slackness. It is negligence of the highest order. You must notify the Victims and Witnesses Unit in good enough time if you expect the witnesses to be here. If you don't, you are not discharging your duty to your client. You are being unprofessional. Do I make myself clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I -- if I may just --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour -- just a second. If you're going to call me unprofessional, then I call this Court on giving me not the resources to get my job done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have cut you off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. I have cut you off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have cut you off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have cut you off, Mr. -- you are totally off.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It is entirely your fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Entirely your fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]... and the time we have. We have not been given the requisite time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you have not done the best you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is clear to me this Court believes that I am privately retained. It is clear to me you think I have a staff of -- of lackeys that are being paid by Mr. Lukic. It is clear to me that this bribery allegation -- [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have cut you off --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have cut you off. I have cut you off because I find your remarks to be totally inappropriate. That is a matter that has been already dealt with by the Trial Chamber and dealt with in a manner entirely favorable to you. I insisted on it being dealt with in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Favorable to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We did not find that the contempt had any merit in it, and I insisted on saying that we found not one scintilla of evidence to implicate you or any of your colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, but you realize -- [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So I will not hear anything more from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, let me -- let me -- let me tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Nothing more from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What I would like to do, Your Honour, is introduce you to my case -- the person that was -- [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are not going to introduce me to anything. We are going to adjourn now, and you will take this warning from me. You will take this warning from me that you are here to represent Mr. Milan Lukic. You have not been ready to present his case. It is entirely your fault. I find that it is entirely your fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Notification, as was just stated by Mr. De Witt, was entirely too late for witnesses to be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I agree with that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you are serious -- if are sufficiently serious in discharging your duty to your client, you would not have informed the Victims and Witnesses Unit on Friday with the expectation, with any reasonable expectation that they would have witnesses here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, and I must correct the record because that is absolutely a misrepresentation. Mr. Markovic was a witness that had been noticed for the week prior, Your Honours. After the hearing on Tuesday, we found out we were going to have court on Monday. That very next day, we started the process of getting more witnesses in addition to Mr. Markovic. Mr. Markovic's papers were all in order, so yes, he could come here within two days. As a matter of fact, Victims and Witnesses --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down, please. Slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to travel. That's today, to travel. So we did discharge our duties. I went from Thursday till last night --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The counsel is kindly asked to slow down for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I went from last Thursday traveling to the area to meet with witnesses to prepare them, not only for this week but for the ongoing witnesses after this week, Your Honour. I came back at 11.00 last night in order to discharge my duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The problem I find with that, you're talking about what you are doing now. What about the time before? All the time that has gone before?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you begin to prepare your defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- when you are called on to present your defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In this case, yes, Your Honour, because of the circumstances that we had. How could we do it before?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is -- that is nonsense and totally unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Totally unprofessional.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I've cut you off. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please stop. Stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you find it a horrible burden and you don't think you can discharge it, then you know what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't want to tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone cut off]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to adjourn now. Legal counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it looks as though we will have to adjourn until Wednesday morning, but let me say this before we do. On the 18th of November, the Chamber ordered Milan Lukic's Defence to begin its case immediately following that of Sredoje Lukic. Sredoje Lukic closed his case on the 2nd of December. Milan Lukic Defence, however, was not ready to begin its case on the 3rd of December. The Chamber adjourned the proceedings until 9 December, but again, the Milan Lukic Defence was not ready to open its case. The Chamber therefore adjourned the proceedings for a second time to today's hearing. Let us move to public session, and I'll begin again. You may both sit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the 18th of December, the Chamber ordered the Defence of Milan Lukic to begin its case immediately following that of Sredoje Lukic. The Defence of Sredoje Lukic closed on the 2nd of December, but Milan Lukic was not ready to present his case on the 3rd of December. Trial Chamber adjourned the proceedings until the 9th of December, but again, the Milan Lukic Defence was not ready to open its case. The Trial Chamber, therefore, has adjourned the proceedings for a second time to today's hearing. In our view, no efforts have been made to comply with the Chamber's order of the 18th of November. The two adjournments have been the result of the failure of the Milan Lukic Defence to comply with the Chamber's orders, to commence presentation of its case on the 3rd and 9th December. As a consequence, a total of six sitting days have been lost. The Chamber is of the view that these two instances of failure by counsel to comply with specific directions have obstructed the proper conduct of the proceedings. Should there be any further repetition, the Chamber will be required to consider what is the appropriate course of action to take pursuant to the Rules of Procedure. The Chamber further recalls that on the 2nd and 9th of December, it warned the Defence that when witnesses are scheduled to attend, they will only be excused if good cause is shown. The Defence was reminded that if there is no good cause, the witness's time can be counted against the number of witnesses and the time allocated to the Defence. Therefore, the Chamber rules that the two witnesses scheduled to testify last week will be deducted from the Defence witness allotment, and the Chamber will also deduct the time for these witnesses from the time allocated to the Defence to present its case. The Chamber will still insist on the deadline of the 6th of March for the end of the Defence case. We are going to adjourn now until Wednesday morning when it is expected that we will have a Defence witness to testify on behalf of the accused Milan Lukic. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
